papers.title: Increased frequency of dislocation following total hip arthroplasty for trauma
papers.abstract: Aims The purpose of this study was to compare surgical techniques and postoperative outcomes in an age- and sex-matched cohort of patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) for neck of femur fracture (#NOF) and for osteoarthritis (OA). Methods A single-centre, consecutive series of patients at minimum one-year follow-up following THA for #NOF were compared with a 1:1 age- and sex-matched cohort of patients following THA for osteoarthritis from the same institution. The primary outcome measure was frequency of dislocation at one year postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included rates of all-cause revision, infection, periprosthetic fracture, and mortality at one year and medium-term postoperatively. Cox regression compared medium-term outcomes between groups, accounting for unequal follow-up duration. Results A total of 722 patients were included, with 361 in each group. BMI was greater in the OA group (28.9 kg/m 2 vs 24.7 kg/m 2 ; p < 0.001). Sex, age, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, and comorbidity profile did not differ between groups (p > 0.247). Overall, 151 patients (41.8%) in the #NOF group received dual-mobility implants, compared with eight (2.2%) in the OA group (p < 0.001). Femoral offset was similar between groups (42.6 mm and 42.7 mm, p = 0.892). Dislocation rates were greater in the #NOF group than the OA group at one-year (4.4% vs 1.1%; p = 0.011) and by final follow-up. The one-year rates of periprosthetic fracture, all-cause revision, and mortality were similar between groups (p > 0.340), although risk of mortality was greater by final follow-up after THA for #NOF (hazard ratio 1.577; p = 0.033). Conclusion Despite the more frequent use of dual-mobility implants in THA for #NOF than OA and the otherwise comparable patient demographics and implants used, the risk of early dislocation after THA for #NOF was four times greater than in an age- and sex-matched elective THA cohort. Early postoperative complication rates were otherwise comparable between the groups. Cite this article: Bone Jt Open 2026;7(11):1455–1461.

papers.title: A dual-functional 3D-printed PEKK scaffold with gelatin-heparin/VEGF modification for enhanced mandibular regeneration
papers.abstract: Polyetherketoneketone (PEKK) possesses bone-mimetic mechanical properties, yet its intrinsic biological inertness limits effective osseointegration. To address this limitation, we developed a biofunctionalized porous PEKK scaffold through 3D printing combined with surface modification of a gelatin heparin hydrogel. Cryogel coatings with varied compositions were fabricated using an ice-templating method, enabling the preservation of the scaffold's porous architecture while improving biocompatibility and facilitating vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) loading and sustained release. In vitro studies using human umbilical vein endothelial cells showed that the modified scaffolds significantly enhanced cell adhesion, proliferation, and angiogenic activity compared with unmodified PEKK. VEGF incorporation further promoted endothelial cell behavior and vascularization potential. In vivo evaluation in a rabbit mandibular defect model showed that the composite scaffold markedly enhanced new bone formation and osseointegration. These findings demonstrate that gelatin-heparin hydrogel functionalization combined with VEGF loading effectively improves the biological performance of PEKK scaffolds. This strategy provides a promising approach for enhancing osseointegration and vascularization in mandibular reconstruction, with potential for clinical translation in the treatment of critical-sized bone defects.

papers.title: MANAGEMENT OF MASSIVE ACETABULAR BONE DEFECTS IN REVISION HIP ARTHROPLASTY USING CUSTOM 3D-PRINTED IMPLANTS
papers.abstract: Background: In repeat revision hip arthroplasty, acetabular component loosening, wear-induced osteolysis, and metallosis may be associated with extensive bone loss. Insufficient remaining bone stock compromises structural support and makes stable fixation with standard revision components challenging. Objective: To describe staged reconstruction of massive acetabular defects and the application of custom 3D-printed implants through two clinical cases. Clinical Cases and Methods: Two cases are presented: a 34-year-old man and a 38-year-old woman with a history of hip arthroplasty and repeated revision procedures. Component loosening was accompanied by metallosis and massive acetabular bone defects. The first treatment stage involved implant removal, excision of metallosis-affected periprosthetic soft tissue and bone, and temporary placement of antibiotic-loaded bone cement within the defect. Definitive reconstruction was planned as a separate stage. Computed tomography and three-dimensional modelling were used to assess defect geometry and remaining bone stock, identify implant–bone contact areas, and plan component orientation, the hip centre of rotation, and screw fixation trajectories. Reconstructive Principles: Patient-specific design allows the implant to accommodate the individual defect geometry and obtain fixation in better-preserved regions of host bone. The porous trabecular surface is intended to improve bone–implant interlock and, provided that reliable primary stability is achieved, support subsequent biological integration. Conclusion: Custom 3D-printed acetabular implants offer a reconstructive option for complex massive defects when adequate fixation with conventional components is limited. Accurate preoperative planning, reliable support on remaining host bone, and conditions conducive to osseointegration are central to this approach. Further clinical and radiographic follow-up is required to assess long-term effectiveness.

papers.title: Relative assessment of strontium-zinc-phosphate chemical conversion coatings on titanium for augmenting bioactivity: Effect of microstructure
papers.abstract: Titanium (Ti) and its alloy are widely used in orthopedics and dentistry implants because of their excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility. However, the bioinert surface of Ti implants may lead to osseointegration defects, which requires surface modification to resolve. In this work, bio-functional strontium zinc phosphate coatings denoted as SZP (SrZn 2 (PO 4 ) 2 ) with varying pattern and microstructure are controllably prepared on Ti surfaces via the phosphate chemical conversion (PCC) method. Although distinct micro/nano topographies of coatings can modulate osteoblast responses, the interaction between the micromorphology of Ti-based PCC coatings and osteoblasts remains elusive. To further explore this issue, the biological response of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) on SZP coatings with different microstructure is investigated in this study. The EDS and XRD results show that all the SZP coatings have similar phase composition. In addition, the SZP coating with lamellar structure presents better hydrophilicity and ion release characteristics comparing with that coating with block crystals. In vitro studies demonstrate that both SZP coatings have biocompatibility with BMSCs and significantly enhance cell adhesion, proliferation and differentiation comparing with bare Ti. Specifically, SZP coating with lamellar grains is more beneficial to the early osseointegration. This study shows that optimizing the microstructure of the PCC coating on Ti-based implants is one of the promising strategies for improving their bone integration.

papers.title: A pre-specified surgical-complexity index is associated with a graded increase in periprosthetic joint infection after total knee arthroplasty: a competing-risks analysis using coronal alignment as a negative control
papers.abstract: Prediction of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) relies almost wholly on host factors, and whether the operation itself carries infection risk independent of the patient is unknown. We analyzed 2920 primary TKAs in 2350 patients from a single institution with national joint registry linkage, using death as a competing risk and coronal alignment as a negative-control exposure. A pre-specified surgical-complexity index counted five construct markers at the index operation: constraint, a tibial stem, a femoral stem, a previous implant and a pre-existing extra-articular deformity or fracture. Septic revision was the primary outcome and aseptic revision the control. Fine–Gray subdistribution hazard models with patient-level clustering estimated complexity and, in the paired-radiograph subset, neutral-alignment effects on both outcomes. There were 51 septic and 104 aseptic revisions and 525 deaths over a median follow-up of 7.4 years. Each additional complexity marker raised the subdistribution hazard of PJI (sHR 1.61, 95% CI 1.27–2.04) but not of aseptic revision (sHR 1.06, 95% CI 0.84–1.33); 5-year PJI incidence rose from 1.5% with zero or one marker to 5.9% with two or more. Neutral coronal alignment was protective against aseptic revision (sHR 0.42, 95% CI 0.26–0.67) but null for PJI (sHR 0.87, 95% CI 0.41–1.87). Adjustment for skin-to-skin operative time, available for 93% of the cohort, moved the complexity estimate in the same knees only from 1.58 to 1.55 and attributed 5 % of the effect to operative time. These are observational associations and not causal effects, but surgical exposure merits consideration alongside host factors in infection-risk assessment.

papers.title: Long-term periprosthetic femoral bone loss after cementless total hip arthroplasty: natural history and response to late osteoporosis treatment.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: The long-term course of periprosthetic bone mineral density (BMD) after cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA) and BMD changes during late osteoporosis treatment remain unclear. METHODS: Fifty-eight hips in 44 patients underwent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) > 15 years after cementless THA using a proximally coated tapered stem. Longitudinal changes were assessed in 18 hips (12 patients) with serial DXA obtained within three months, at one year, and at a mean of 17.2 years postoperatively. For therapeutic analysis, ten hips (7 patients) with osteoporosis received zoledronic acid annually, together with daily eldecalcitol and calcium, for two years with serial DXA before treatment and during follow-up. RESULTS: At a mean of 17.2 years, lumbar spine BMD declined to 74.9% of baseline (P < 0.001 vs 1 year). Zones 3-5 showed similar reductions (all P > 0.05, vs lumbar spine). In contrast, proximal zones 1, 2, 6, and 7 showed significantly greater reductions (60.0%, 61.8%, 54.0%, and 30.8%, respectively; all P < 0.001 vs lumbar spine), with zone 7 demonstrating the greatest decrease. During osteoporosis treatment, lumbar spine BMD increased to 107.8% of pretreatment values at two years (P = 0.004). No statistically significant change in periprosthetic BMD was detected, although only zone 5 showed a significant increase (P = 0.014). CONCLUSIONS: Proximal periprosthetic bone loss was evident beyond 15 years after cementless THA, with the greatest reduction in Zone 7. Late osteoporosis treatment was associated with no significant further decline in periprosthetic BMD but did not reverse severe proximal bone loss.

papers.title: Constructing functionalized cartilage organoids by preserving mitochondrial homeostasis to accelerate cartilage repair
papers.abstract: Due to the lack of blood vessels and nerves in cartilage tissue, its regeneration and repair has always been a clinical challenge. Cartilage organoids (COs) are miniature cartilage tissues cultivated using stem cells or chondrocytes, which have a broad application prospect in the field of cartilage regeneration and repair. However, prolonged scaffold-based culture of COs is often accompanied by chondrocyte hypertrophy and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, which may compromise the maintenance of a stable cartilage phenotype. In this study, transcriptomic analysis of COs cultured for up to 8 weeks revealed stage-dependent changes in stress- and matrix-related programs and suggested that altered mitochondrial homeostasis may be associated with phenotypic deterioration. To address this problem, this study constructed a MnO 2 -Melatonin@DNA-SF hydrogel (Mn-Me@DSH) bioink matrix by loading MnO 2 nanoparticles and Melatonin on DNA-SF hydrogels. Subsequently, we bioprinted BMSCs with Mn-Me@DSH using a DLP system to produce a functionalized COs that could maintain mitochondrial homeostasis. These engineered COs effectively repaired cartilage defects in rats within 6 weeks. This study breaks through the limitations of the traditional COs in the oxidative stress microenvironment through the ROS scavenging, and provides a new solution for the construction of functionalized COs and cartilage regeneration.

papers.title: A multi-objective optimization approach based on HBA-RF for lightweight design of automotive rear seats
papers.abstract: In multi-objective optimization design of automotive seats, crashworthiness evaluation is often constrained by the high cost of physical experiments and the time-consuming nature of finite element simulations. Conventional single surrogate models frequently struggle to achieve satisfactory fitting accuracy when dealing with complex nonlinear responses. Moreover, complex engineering multi-objective optimization problems employing high-fidelity simulation models often suffer from excessive computational costs. Integrated surrogate models combining metaheuristic algorithms with surrogate modeling techniques can improve prediction accuracy and robustness; however, their global optimization capability remains challenging and requires efficient metaheuristic solvers. To address the imbalance between global exploration and local exploitation, susceptibility to local optima, and slow convergence of conventional Random Forest (RF) surrogate models, an optimized surrogate model (HBA-RF) is proposed. By incorporating the Honey Badger Algorithm (HBA), the optimization efficiency of the original RF is significantly enhanced, leading to improved global search capability, convergence stability, and overall performance. Based on this model, an integrated optimization framework is developed, incorporating optimal Latin hypercube design (OLHD), HBA-based RF surrogate modeling, the multi-objective grey wolf optimizer (MOGWO), and an MPSI-based decision-making method. To validate the effectiveness of the HBA-RF surrogate model, the trunk impact response of a passenger vehicle rear seat was selected as a test case, and comparative analyses were conducted against several modeling approaches reported in recent literature. For the passenger vehicle rear seat, headrest displacement ( Dis 1 ), seatback displacement ( Dis 2 ), cost, and mass were selected as the primary performance indicators. The proposed framework was further validated through a multi-objective lightweight optimization problem of the rear seat, demonstrating its feasibility and effectiveness in practical engineering applications. The optimization results indicate that, compared with the original design, the seatback mass is reduced by 3.46%, successfully achieving the lightweight design objective. In terms of performance, the headrest displacement ( Dis 1 ) is reduced by 5.05%, while the seatback displacement ( Dis 2 ) decreases slightly by 3.83%. Meanwhile, the cost decreases from 49.02 (¥) to 48.226 (¥), corresponding to a reduction of 1.62%. Simulation results confirm that all prediction errors remain within acceptable limits and that all performance indicators satisfy the predefined development targets for the rear seat. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method effectively balances lightweight design, cost, and safety performance, fulfilling the multi-objective optimization requirements of a passenger vehicle rear seat frame while highlighting its robustness and engineering practicality.

papers.abstract: Bridge-type compliant mechanisms (BCMs) are widely utilized in micro- and nano-positioning systems for motion amplification. Balancing performance across amplification capability, stiffness, stress, and structural compactness for a BCM is challenging because of the coupled and competing effects among these performance metrics. This paper presents an integrated framework that combines surrogate modeling, multi-objective optimization, and multi-criteria decision-making for the application-specific optimization of BCMs. Geometric parameterization of the BCM is established to enable fast, automated finite element analysis. Optimal Latin hypercube sampling (OLHS) is used to generate the BCM sample set, whose pairwise correlations are assessed through correlation analysis. Based on the sample responses, the surrogate model with the highest predictive accuracy is selected from RSM, RBF, SVR, and Kriging. Four multi-objective optimization algorithms, MOPSO, SPEA2, NSGA-II, and NSGA-III, are compared in terms of convergence, solution distribution, and coverage to select the algorithm for subsequent optimization. The resulting Pareto solutions are ranked using AHP–EWM combined with TOPSIS. The framework is applied to the series design of three BCMs intended to provide graded output stiffnesses. The optimized designs are verified through finite element analysis and experimental study. The results demonstrate that the framework balances competing performance requirements and facilitates application-oriented series design of BCMs.

papers.title: Experimental Validation of Calibration Constants Determined by a Deep Operator Network for IHD in Laminated Composite Materials
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The incremental hole-drilling technique requires calibration constants to relate the measured strain data to the residual stress distribution that existed in the material prior to drilling. For laminated composite materials, the calibration constants must be determined individually from finite element (FE) analyses for the specific combination of laminate configuration, material properties and experimental parameters used. Depending on the computational method and uncertainty sources considered, hundreds of FE analyses may be required per laminate configuration. This can become burdensome, especially if numerous laminate configurations are under investigation. A type of neural network known as a deep operator network (DeepONet) offers the potential to significantly reduce the amount of computation required. Objective Investigate the use of a DeepONet to predict calibration constants for the integral method applied to balanced and symmetric fibre reinforced plastic (FRP) laminates of eight plies aligned at 0 $$^\circ $$ ∘ , $$90^\circ $$ 90 ∘ , +45 $$^\circ $$ ∘ or -45 $$^\circ $$ ∘ . Methods The DeepONet model was trained on the FE predicted top surface displacement fields, for every stress application depth and drilling increment, of 15 of the 70 possible E-glass/epoxy FRP laminate configurations. IHD was performed on two specimens, one each of [90 2 /0 2 ] s and [0 2 /+45/-45] s configuration, which were not part of the training set. Results The residual stress distributions obtained using DeepONet predicted and FE generated calibration constants showed good agreement, $$\approx $$ ≈ 1 – 1.5 MPa, over the measurement depth. Conclusions The agreement in the calculated residual stress distributions demonstrates that the calibration constants predicted by the DeepONet model have acceptable accuracy for practical application, $$\approx $$ ≈ 10%, while significantly reducing the amount of FE analyses required.

papers.title: Bone Retention Without Osseointegration During Antiresorptive Therapy: A Rat Model of Immediate Implant Placement Following Prolonged Ligature-Induced Periodontitis
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Immediate implant placement in sites with prolonged ligature-induced periodontal disease during antiresorptive therapy is poorly modeled. This study investigated whether zoledronic acid (ZA) could preserve peri-implant bone sufficiently to support osseointegration in a rat challenge model. Methods: Thirty-two adult male Wistar rats received saline (SAL) or ZA (ZOL). Ligature-induced periodontitis was maintained for seven weeks around the mandibular first molar, followed by extraction and immediate placement of a commercially pure titanium implant. Animals were euthanized after 28 days. Removal torque (RTQ), SEM-EDX, and micro-computed tomography were assessed alongside undecalcified histology, which underwent qualitative evaluation and blinded exploratory semiquantitative scoring. Results: Median RTQ and peri-implant bone volume fraction (BV/TV) were numerically higher in ZOL than SAL animals (RTQ: 4.0 vs. 2.5 N·cm, p = 0.104; BV/TV: 46.5% vs. 28.0%, p = 0.113), but neither difference reached statistical significance. Histology showed near-complete absence of new bone–implant contact, with median scores of 0 in both groups. Compared with SAL, ZOL specimens showed descriptively greater retention of alveolar architecture, while 4 of 8 specimens had no detectable viable bone in the assessed peri-implant region. Epithelial coverage scores were lower in ZOL than in SAL (median: 0 vs. 2; nominal p = 0.027). Conclusions: Under the combined experimental conditions, retention of peri-implant mineralized tissue did not correspond to meaningful regenerative osseointegration. The findings distinguish bone quantity and mechanical anchorage from direct biological integration and should not be extrapolated directly to routine clinical implant therapy.

papers.title: 3D Bioprinting as an In Vitro Tool to Model the Tumor Microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Three‑dimensional (3D) bioprinting has rapidly emerged as a powerful strategy for engineering physiologically relevant tumor microenvironment (TME) models that overcome the limitations of traditional 2D cultures and animal systems. The TME is a highly dynamic and heterogeneous ecosystem composed of malignant, stromal, immune, and vascular cells embedded within a biochemically and mechanically complex extracellular matrix (ECM). These components collectively regulate tumor progression, immune evasion, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. Conventional preclinical models fail to capture this complexity, contributing to poor clinical translation of oncology therapeutics. Advances in extrusion‑based, inkjet, laser‑assisted, and stereolithographic bioprinting now enable spatially organized, multicellular constructs with tunable biochemical and biophysical cues that more accurately recapitulate TME architecture and function. Complementary innovations in biomaterials, microfluidics, and computational modeling further expand the capabilities of bioprinted systems for drug screening, mechanistic studies, and personalized medicine. This review summarizes the cellular and acellular components of the TME, outlines major bioprinting technologies and biomaterial strategies, and highlights emerging applications in cancer modeling. We also identify key research gaps and opportunities that must be addressed to advance bioprinted TME platforms toward robust, standardized, and clinically meaningful tools for precision oncology.

papers.title: Assessing the Accuracy of Bayesian-Optimized CGMD in Predicting Polymer Miscibility
papers.abstract: Abstract Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) presents a computationally efficient alternative to all-atom (AA) simulations for modeling polymer systems, yet the accuracy of its predictions for emergent thermodynamic properties remains a challenge. This study builds upon our previous work, which introduced a Bayesian optimization framework for refining Martini3 force field, to validate the transferability of these optimized models to multi-component systems. We demonstrate that CG force fields, optimized against single-chain properties (density and radius of gyration), can qualitatively estimate the phase behavior of both homopolymer blends and diblock copolymer systems. Bayesian-optimized topologies for polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), polystyrene (PS), and poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) were evaluated through direct simulation of binary blend morphologies and a PMMA-PEO (poly(ethylene oxide)) diblock copolymer system. The framework successfully predicted macroscopic phase separation in the immiscible PS-PMMA system and miscibility in the PVDF-PMMA system, with resulting density profiles showing qualitative agreement with experimental observations. Flory–Huggins interaction parameters ( $$\chi $$ χ ) estimated from Hildebrand solubility parameters ( $$\delta $$ δ ) correctly rank relative miscibilities and align qualitatively with literature trends. Our results show that optimizing for fundamental properties such as density and radius of gyration (achieving <10% error) implicitly captures the necessary thermodynamic contributions to predict complex, multi-component phase behaviors. Validation of miscibility prediction across two canonical homopolymer blends, combined with efficient parameterization of a diblock copolymer architecture, provides compelling evidence that Bayesian-optimized coarse-grained molecular dynamics is a robust and predictive tool for polymer thermodynamics, effectively bridging the gap between computational efficiency and predictive fidelity in materials discovery.

papers.title: Using Machine Learning to Compute Constrained Optimal Carbon Tax Rules
papers.abstract: We develop a computational framework for deriving Pareto-improving and constrained optimal carbon tax rules in a stochastic overlapping generations (OLG) model with climate change. By integrating Deep Equilibrium Networks for fast policy evaluation and Gaussian process surrogate modeling with Bayesian active learning, the framework systematically locates optimal carbon tax schedules for heterogeneous agents exposed to climate risk. We apply our method to a 12-period OLG model in which exogenous shocks affect the carbon intensity of energy production, as well as the damage function. Constrained optimal carbon taxes consist of tax rates that are simple functions of observables and revenue-sharing rules that guarantee that the introduction of the taxes is Pareto improving. This reveals that a straightforward policy is highly effective: a Pareto-improving linear tax on cumulative emissions alone yields a 0.42% aggregate welfare gain in consumption-equivalent terms while adding further complexity to the tax provides only a marginal increase to 0.45%. The application demonstrates that the proposed approach produces scalable tools for macro-policy design in complex stochastic settings. Beyond climate economics, the framework offers a template for systematically analyzing welfare-improving policies in various heterogeneous-agent problems.

papers.title: Technical note: Integrating generative AI with physics-based simulations for probabilistic modelling of volcanic clouds
papers.abstract: Ensemble-based modelling of the atmospheric dispersal of volcanic clouds enables more realistic forecasts by explicitly accounting for uncertainties in eruption source parameters, meteorological data, and systematic errors in transport models. Many ensemble applications, including forecast uncertainty quantification, data assimilation, and probabilistic hazard assessment, require large ensembles to reduce sampling errors and adequately represent probability distributions. However, simulating and processing large ensembles with atmospheric dispersal models can be computationally demanding, even on high-performance computing clusters. Generative AI offers a complementary approach by representing simulated fields in a lower-dimensional latent space, enabling new samples to be generated at low computational cost and facilitating the manipulation of large ensembles. A Variational AutoEncoder (VAE) is trained on ensembles of physics-based simulations and used to generate new samples. The learned latent-space representation is then used to test two ensemble-based data assimilation methods, demonstrating the potential benefits of performing data assimilation in a lower-dimensional space. As a proof of concept, the data assimilation problem is formulated in two dimensions. Two numerical experiments demonstrate that VAE-generated ensembles can reproduce key statistics of a larger reference ensemble and improve agreement with satellite retrievals. The VAE achieves up to a 1000-fold compression of the original fields into 16- and 32-dimensional latent spaces. The VAE-generated ensemble of 4096 members reduces RMSE by 4 % relative to the model prior, while latent-space data assimilation further reduces RMSE by 30 %. papers.title: Real-time machine learning control of a Hall thruster discharge plasma
papers.abstract: Facility effects are known to alter Hall thruster performance between ground and space. Furthermore, discharge current oscillations are linked to impacting both the lifetime and thrust of Hall thrusters. In this work, we present a machine learning–based control framework designed for nonlinear, time-varying systems with hysteresis that can mitigate BM oscillations and adapt to environmental changes. Unlike reactive approaches such as PID control, our method is predictive and flexible across a range of control objectives. Specifically, we employ echo state networks (ESNs), a class of recurrent neural networks well-suited for time-series prediction. To train and test the model, we apply a diverse set of discharge voltage perturbations—including sine, triangle, square, ramp, chirp, bandlimited gaussian noise, pseudorandom binary sequence, and PID—on a 6-kW H6 Hall thruster operated at 400 V as well as 250 V at 4.3 A, and measure the resulting discharge current as a part of a process known as system identification. We found that 34 VRMS Gaussian noise perturbations can reduce discharge current oscillations locally by 84.6%, making them an ideal system identification signal. Using extended convergent cross mapping, we confirm causal relationships between the applied perturbations and discharge current response. The ESN achieves 90% prediction accuracy on previously unseen time-series data based on variance. We then integrate the ESN into a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) framework, creating a machine learning controller, to compute optimal control trajectories that suppress discharge oscillations. NMPC simulations indicate that discharge current oscillations can be reduced by over 90%. Finally, we employ a deployment strategy in which the learned control policy is embedded as a multilayer perceptron (MLP) on a field-programmable gate array, enabling real-time experimental implementation. The machine learning (ML) controller utilizing the MLP reduces oscillations by 1.33% while PID increases oscillations by 1.44% at the 250 V operating point. The ML controller has the potential to be applicable to other operating points by following a standard procedure of system identification and control optimization. Online and adaptive ML control can be used in the future to improve oscillation reduction.

papers.title: Probabilistic Voltage Harmonic Compliance-Margin Forecasting with Adaptive Conformal Prediction at Low-Voltage Distribution Points of Common Coupling
papers.abstract: Increasing deployment of power-electronic loads has intensified the need for short-horizon forecasting of voltage harmonic distortion at low-voltage points of common coupling. This study develops a telemetry-first framework for forecasting phase-wise voltage total harmonic distortion (UTHD) and its compliance margin using routinely retained 10 min power-quality indices. Independent histogram-based gradient-boosting regressors (HGBRs) were trained for 10, 30, 60, and 120 min horizons using leakage-controlled chronological validation and were benchmarked against persistence, seasonal and climatological references, Ridge, autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), target-history-only HGBR, XGBoost, and LightGBM. Forecast uncertainty was quantified using symmetric conformal prediction with calibration-only selection of adaptive residual parameters. Across the three Córdoba phases, the common-feature HGBR achieved mean MAEs of 0.198, 0.225, 0.232, and 0.258 percentage points at 10, 30, 60, and 120 min, respectively, and consistently outperformed persistence. The selected conformal configuration achieved mean empirical coverages of 90.55–88.77% for nominal 90% intervals and 95.15–94.17% for nominal 95% intervals across increasing horizons. These findings show that index-level telemetry can support accurate multi-horizon UTHD forecasting with empirically calibrated predictive uncertainty for forecast-informed harmonic monitoring.

papers.title: Beyond Teacher Certification: A CIPP Evaluation of Curriculum Implementation in an Indonesian Elementary School
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the enactment of the Merdeka Curriculum in a public elementary school in Ambon, Indonesia, using the context, input, process, and product (CIPP) framework. A qualitative, decision-oriented case evaluation was undertaken on 7–8 May 2026. Evidence reported in the original study comprised interviews with the principal and teachers, classroom observations, school-document review, and photographs of facilities. Findings revealed a persistent implementation gap across the four evaluation dimensions. In the context dimension, approximately 85% of pupils were reported to come from lower- to middle-income households, alongside limited parental engagement. In the input dimension, eight of ten teachers held professional certification, and basic teaching materials were available, but instructional plans and digital equipment were not consistently used to support active learning. In the process dimension, approximately 80% of observed or reported instruction was described as teacher-centred, formative assessment was inconsistent, and principal-led classroom supervision occurred once annually. In the product dimension, approximately 70% of pupils reportedly exceeded the school’s learning-objective attainment criteria, despite teachers’ concerns about literacy, numeracy, attendance, and discipline. The main contribution is an evidence-bounded diagnosis of the discontinuity between formal teacher qualifications and enacted pedagogy. The findings support prioritising instructional coaching, formative assessment, targeted foundational-skills support, and school–family collaboration. Given the two-day, single-site design and incomplete quantitative denominators, the reported proportions are descriptive rather than generalisable estimates.

papers.title: Neuroeducation and artificial intelligence: innovative strategies to strengthen teaching and learning processes in Basic General Education
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into basic general education creates new possibilities for differentiated teaching, while neuroeducation contributes evidence on attention, memory, motivation, self-regulation, and learning. This documentary review aimed to examine pedagogical strategies derived from both fields and assess their opportunities and limitations in school teaching and learning. A targeted search of academic literature published between January 2020 and August 31, 2026 was conducted using thematic relevance, editorial traceability, and educational applicability criteria. PRISMA 2020 guidance informed transparent reporting of the selection process, without claiming an undocumented exhaustive quantitative flow. The synthesis drew on 16 verified academic publications and four methodological or institutional sources. Findings were organized into four dimensions: neuroeducational principles, AI-supported personalization, teacher competencies, and ethical implementation conditions. Reviewed studies suggest opportunities for differentiated feedback, graduated tasks, active learning, and lesson planning. However, they also identify persistent neuromyths, variable accuracy of generative outputs, children’s data privacy risks, and unequal access to digital infrastructure. The review concludes that combining neuroeducation and AI can be pedagogically relevant when AI remains a supervised support tool, measurable learning outcomes are assessed, and technological personalization is not confused with neurocognitive diagnosis. Teacher judgment, inclusion, and evidence-based instructional design should guide implementation.

papers.title: A Topological Network Model for Wafer Map Defect Recognition Based on Persistent Homology Features and Bayesian Threshold Optimization
papers.abstract: Wafer map defect recognition depends on shape, which makes persistent homology a natural representation, but existing topological treatments have been validated on synthetic maps whose defect rings are intact. We evaluate the representation on the real WM-811K benchmark under lot-disjoint evaluation. The novelty is threefold: a valid-die-mask filtration with an explicit, per-wafer stability constant, the use of that constant to turn threshold selection into a constrained problem, and a density-controlled test of which barcode summaries carry shape. The mask is necessary—a cubical complex on the raw array manufactures topology outside the wafer—and so is the choice of summary: total H1 persistence proxies the fraction of dies that failed and loses its association with the cyclic classes once that density is controlled for, whereas the dominant-loop share retains it. Those classes, Donut and Edge-Ring, are the only cyclic classes that WM-811K labels, and Donut spans only 233 lots, so this is a statement about them and not about cyclic defects in general. The die-flip stability bound we prove defines an admissible set of truncation levels, searched by Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization—a mechanism for solving that constrained problem, not a search strategy shown to beat random or grid search at equal budget. The guarantee is delimited: it governs which persistence bars survive truncation under a k-die perturbation, and covers neither the remaining feature coordinates nor any classifier’s predictions. Certified truncation costs 2.88 points of macro-F1 for the topological model [1.88,3.91] and 0.52 for the fusion model, whose interval includes zero. Fusing the two representations beats a capacity-matched convolutional model by 1.46 points with fewer parameters [0.78,2.18], and beats its own permutation control. Two design choices preceded the partition and enter only the topological branch, so these margins are upper estimates this design cannot correct. At 25 labeled wafers per class, the topological representation leads by 13.5 points [12.19,14.71]; by 400, the ordering has reversed. Lot-disjoint evaluation removes within-benchmark lot correlation; it does not establish transfer to another fab or acquisition process.

papers.title: Investigation of Solid Particle Erosion Wear Behavior of Additively Manufactured AlSi10Mg Alloys Under Cryogenic Conditions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study comparatively investigates the solid particle erosion behavior of cast and laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)‐manufactured AlSi10Mg alloys under room‐temperature and cryogenic conditions, including the effect of T6 heat treatment. Erosion tests were conducted according to ASTM G76 using SiC particles (∼350 µm) at 3 bar and six impact angles (15°–90°). For cryogenic tests, specimens were immersed in liquid nitrogen, and erosion experiments were completed, whereas the surface temperature remained below −100°C. Erosion performance was quantified by weight loss, whereas damage mechanisms were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and three‐dimensional surface topography. Discrete element method (DEM) simulations were additionally performed to examine particle impact behavior. The results demonstrated a strong dependence of erosion rate on impact angle. LPBF‐manufactured specimens generally exhibited higher erosion resistance than their cast counterparts, whereas the influence of T6 heat treatment depended on the manufacturing route. Conversely, cryogenic conditions generally increased material loss. Surface analyses showed predominantly ductile erosion mechanisms, characterized by cutting, plowing, lip, and crater formation, and localized plastic deformation, with no extensive brittle fracture. These findings demonstrate the combined effects of manufacturing route, heat treatment, and cryogenic exposure on the erosion response of AlSi10Mg.

papers.abstract: Abstract Improving operational safety under fluctuating wind-solar power input constitutes a critical challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) technology, and developing an efficient and fast operating condition regulation method is an important approach to address this challenge. Nevertheless, the widely adopted proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control method relies heavily on manual tuning experience, which renders it incapable of precisely regulating the strongly nonlinear and tightly coupled electrolysis process and brings risks of temperature overshoot and response lag. Therefore, an online adaptive temperature regulation method for electrolyzer integrating an electro-thermal-mass performance prediction model with an adaptive model predictive control (AMPC) algorithm is proposed. The electro-thermal-mass performance prediction model comprehensively accounts for electric conduction, heat transfer, and multi-phase mass transport. Meanwhile, the control algorithm supports real-time updating of electrolyzer operating states. The performance prediction model is validated through experimental tests on a 100 kW PEM electrolyzer. Results show that the proposed model achieves a temperature prediction accuracy of 5.3%. It is also found that circulating cooling water temperature varies more mildly than water flow rate, so it is more applicable to temperature regulation under dynamic operating conditions. A comparison of control performance is conducted between the proposed AMPC method and the PID control method to verify the effectiveness of the adaptive regulation strategy. Results indicate that the AMPC method shortens the temperature rise response time by 0.55 h. Under simulated fluctuating wind-solar power input conditions, the AMPC method can adjust the electrolyzer temperature to the target value within 10.7 min, with the temperature overshoot 4.2 °C lower than that of PID control. This research is expected to provide theoretical references and technical tools for the safe and reliable application of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis technology in future large-scale direct wind-solar coupled hydrogen production systems.

papers.title: Self-Repairing Predictive Control for Selective Catalytic Reduction Systems Based on Slow Feature Analysis and Closed-Loop Subspace Identification
papers.abstract: Model–plant mismatch can impair predictive control of selective catalytic reduction (SCR) systems as operating conditions and process dynamics change. This study develops a self-repairing model predictive control (MPC) framework integrating slow-feature analysis (SFA), short-duration input excitation, and optimized predictor-based subspace identification (PBSIDopt). Its contribution is the coordinated monitoring–excitation–identification–validation–updating procedure rather than a new SFA or identification algorithm. A candidate model is accepted only after an independent multistep-prediction test and model/controller checks; the predictor, controller, and residual monitor are then updated together. Four representative simulations examine abrupt mismatch, two rates of gradual mismatch, and a different parameter-change direction. Relative to fixed-model MPC, the SFA framework reduced whole-run mean absolute tracking error by 5.63–42.91% and final-interval error by 24.07–69.08%. Compared with an exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) monitor embedded in the same repair framework, SFA yielded lower whole-run tracking errors in three of the four representative scenarios. These illustrative simulation results support the feasibility of the integrated framework; they do not establish universal monitoring superiority or long-term industrial safety.

papers.title: Nonlinear model predictive control for lateral path tracking of intelligent vehicles considering model uncertainties
papers.abstract: Under critical maneuvers like high-speed emergency steering, conventional Linear Model Predictive Control (LMPC) suffers from insufficient path-tracking accuracy, owing to coupled effects of multiple sources of model uncertainties -including model simplification errors, parameter perturbations, and unmodeled dynamics, as well as a limited capability to characterize highly nonlinear vehicle dynamics, which may even lead to safety issues like trajectory deviation or instability of intelligent vehicles. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a Model Uncertainty-Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (MU-NMPC) algorithm for lateral path tracking that accounts for model uncertainties. The framework initiates by establishing a Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) structure using a nonlinear two-degree-of-freedom (2DOF) vehicle model, which is solved via Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP). Furthermore, a state-error-based uncertainty compensation mechanism is developed to mitigate model uncertainties through online closed-loop feedback identification and real-time filtering for prediction errors estimation. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed MU-NMPC algorithm is verified through both simulations tests and SpeedGoat-based rapid control prototyping (RCP) experiments. Compared with LMPC, MU-NMPC exhibits superior performance under extreme conditions: it not only maintains sufficient control margins and enhances the vehicle’s emergency handling capability but also significantly improves path-tracking accuracy. Moreover, in the presence of parameter variations such as ±20% perturbations in vehicle mass and moment of inertia, MU-NMPC effectively suppresses the rate of change in path tracking error, demonstrating strong robustness performance in complex operational scenarios.

papers.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates accurate electrochemical parameter identification in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer systems (PEMWES), which is essential for multiphysics digital twins and dynamic control. Conventional analytical and metaheuristic methods may suffer from numerical instability, parameter coupling, and high computational latency under coupled thermal and pressure variations. Purely data-driven models may lack physical interpretability and electrochemical consistency, motivating the proposed BO-LSBoost framework for parameter identification and residual correction. Five core parameters ( $$\:\varDelta\:G,\:J₀,\:\alpha\:,\:r,\:\:{J}_{L}$$ ) are identified for a 160 cm² single-cell electrolyzer operating at 50–80 ( $$\: {}^{ \circ }C $$ )and pressures up to 30 bars. Bayesian Optimization (BO) estimates global thermodynamic and kinetic parameters, while Least-Squares Gradient Boosting (LSBoost) compensates for unmodelled multiphysics residuals. The model achieves mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 0.0006% and 0.0014% for thermal and pressure sweeps, respectively. Dynamic cycling yields an average absolute voltage error of 0.01 V. Increasing the sample size from N = 60 to 239 reduces MAPE from 0.0335% to 0.0028%, demonstrating improved prediction accuracy for real-time load emulation.

papers.abstract: Population aging, dependency, and demand for long-term care call for improvements in employment quality and greater social and labor inclusion of women in situations of vulnerability. It was designed within EDIMET, Decent Employment for Migrant Women in the Cross-Border Area (0531_EDIMET_3_E), funded by Interreg Spain–Portugal (POCTEP) 2021–2027, and connects decent work with the prevention of labor exploitation. The pathway integrates the legal framework and literature on the social economy, cooperatives, entrepreneurship, vulnerability, care, and inclusion. It combines personal, relational, cooperative, entrepreneurial, technical and organizational, legal and administrative, and digital and management competencies; modules on cooperative design and management, home help, accreditation, and support; and active learning methods, projects, simulations, tutoring, and continuous assessment. A curriculum design is presented with potential for adaptation by training providers, public administrations, and social economy organizations. Its contribution lies in connecting the recognition of competencies, group support, the professionalization of care, and the prevention of exploitation. Design validation, feasibility, acceptability, learning outcomes, and social and employment effects require subsequent evaluation

papers.title: An NMPC-Based False-Cue-Suppressing Motion Cueing Algorithm for 9-DoF Motion Simulators
papers.abstract: Motion cueing algorithms reproduce the perceived motion of vehicles within the limited workspace of driving and flight simulators. Nine-DoF simulators enlarge this workspace considerably yet expose three difficulties: rectangular task space envelopes leave much of the reachable set unused, sustained accelerations produce vestibular false cues, and the nonlinear per-stage linearization of model predictive control is the real-time bottleneck. To address these difficulties, this paper proposes separate strategies within a nonlinear model predictive cueing algorithm for such platforms. Constraints are imposed directly on the leg lengths obtained from the kinematic inverse, replacing the rectangular envelope and making the full reachable workspace available. A deadband penalty, referenced to vestibular perception thresholds and the current reference magnitude, suppresses cues that contradict the reference in sign. Finally, the Newton–Euler dynamics are approximated by an extended dynamic mode decomposition model with a neural network residual, which turns per-stage linearization into a constant-matrix read, shortening the solving time to meet the real-time control requirement at an acceptable accuracy cost. Closed-loop simulations on four flight maneuver classes show sustained false cues driven back below the perception threshold while the reachable workspace is fully exploited.

papers.title: Combinatorial Inference on the Optimal Assortment in Multinomial Logit Models
papers.abstract: Assortment optimization has been extensively explored in recent decades due to its practical significance. Despite the substantial literature on optimization algorithms and latent score estimation, there remains a need to explore uncertainty quantification for the optimal assortment. Instead of estimating and recovering the complete optimal offer set, decision-makers may be interested in testing whether a given property holds for the optimal assortment. For instance, they may wish to determine whether certain products of interest should be included in the optimal set or ascertain how many categories of products the optimal set should contain. This paper proposes a novel inferential framework for testing such properties within the context of the widely adopted multinomial logit (MNL) model. In this model, each customer is assumed to purchase an item within the offered products with a probability proportional to the underlying preference score associated with the product. We reduce inferring a general optimal assortment property to quantifying the uncertainty associated with the sign change point detection of the marginal revenue gaps. We establish the asymptotic normality of the marginal revenue gap estimator and construct a maximum statistic using the gap estimators to detect the sign change point. By approximating the distribution of the maximum statistic through multiplier bootstrap techniques, we propose a valid testing procedure. Numerical experiments are also conducted to assess the performance of our method.

papers.title: A review of uncertainty quantification for dam deformation prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract Dams are critical infrastructure for flood control and water resource regulation, and their safe operation is essential to public safety and socioeconomic development. Among various monitoring indicators, deformation is widely regarded as a key metric reflecting structural behavior, making its accurate prediction crucial for structural health assessment. Currently, data-driven deformation prediction models have been widely applied owing to their strong nonlinear fitting capabilities. However, these models typically provide deterministic point predictions only and fail to characterize uncertainties arising from the coupled effects of material deterioration, hydrological and environmental loading disturbances, model approximation, and monitoring noise during long-term operation. This limitation reduces the reliability of deformation predictions and weakens their support for structural safety assessment. Consequently, uncertainty quantification (UQ) has emerged as a critical approach to improving the credibility of deformation predictions. This review analyzes the primary sources of uncertainty in dam deformation prediction. Existing UQ approaches are classified into two main groups, non-Bayesian and Bayesian methods, according to whether uncertainty estimation relies on Bayesian posterior inference. Their methodological characteristics, strengths, and limitations are discussed, and key challenges and future research directions are identified, with the aim of supporting more reliable deformation prediction and structural safety assessment under uncertainty.

papers.title: Dimensionality-guided sparse sampling for time-domain thermoreflectance: high-throughput thermal mapping of multilayer devices
papers.abstract: Thermal characterization of multilayer microelectronic devices requires efficient measurement strategies that balance accuracy against investigation resources. Time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) offers non-contact thermal property measurement, yet conventional approaches rely on densely sampled data and prior knowledge of material properties. We address these limitations through a data-driven framework combining dimensionality analysis with measurement optimization. Using an autoencoder, we reveal that across the broad range of bilayer systems in the diffusive regime, TDTR signals exhibit a low dimensionality: three degrees of freedom for single-frequency measurements, four for multifrequency measurements. Guided by this limit, Bayesian optimization identifies a nine-point sparse sampling configuration that captures information equivalent to 192-point scans. A neural network trained on this configuration enables simultaneous extraction of film thickness, thermal conductivity, and interfacial conductance where sensitivity permits. We validate the framework on SiO 2 /Si specimens and demonstrate its utility by mapping multilayer ceramic capacitors. Our approach achieves thermal property mapping without prior knowledge of the sample structure, transforming TDTR into a high-throughput image modality.

papers.abstract: Wind and photovoltaic (PV) fluctuations and forecast errors create a need for coordinated peak-shaving dispatch. This study develops a hierarchical intraday–period-level scheduling model. The intraday layer maximizes net system profit by jointly accounting for electricity revenue, differentiated peak-shaving compensation, operating costs, and renewable-curtailment penalties and provides power and storage-energy reference schedules. The period-level layer applies model predictive control (MPC) with a 1 min control interval and a 15 min prediction horizon to minimize schedule-tracking error subject to power-balance, equipment, and storage-energy constraints. An improved hybrid Aquila Optimizer–African Vultures Optimization Algorithm (IHAEAVOA) searches for dispatch solutions. Two case studies, with wind generation without PV and PV generation without wind, examine power coordination, storage states, and economic outcomes. Coordinated dispatch yields net profits of USD 12,622.76 and USD 7232.42, compared with USD 4351.16 and USD 5467.41 for intraday-only dispatch, while curtailment rates reach 0.001% and 0.01%, respectively. These results illustrate the coordination of economic reference scheduling and short-horizon tracking within the specified scenarios and model boundaries. By improving renewable energy utilization while maintaining economic performance, the framework supports sustainable power system operation under the studied conditions.

papers.title: Trajectory planning for autonomous semi-trailer vehicles based on EDT constraints
papers.abstract: Real-time trajectory planning for autonomous semi-trailer vehicles is challenging because tractor–trailer coupling and trailer tail-swing make it difficult to simultaneously ensure kinematic feasibility, obstacle clearance, motion smoothness, and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a trajectory-planning method with Euclidean distance transform (EDT) constraints that combines motion-primitive graph search with online nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC). The graph-search stage generates a collision-free initial trajectory satisfying the tractor–trailer kinematic constraints, while the Euclidean distance transform converts discrete obstacle information into continuous clearance information. The EDT distance field is incorporated into NMPC as both a soft obstacle-avoidance cost and a hard minimum-distance constraint. Simulation results in structured and unstructured environments show that the proposed method provides larger safety margins and smoother trajectories than the timed elastic band (TEB) planner, while reducing fluctuations in the tractor steering angle and trailer articulation angle. The average planning times are 33 and 37 ms, respectively. Real-vehicle experiments further verify the practical executability of the planned trajectories.

This study employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive method. The research subjects consisted of two teachers and five eleventh-grade students at SMK Swasta Delisha. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation. Data analysis involved data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Data validity was established through source triangulation and technique triangulation. The findings revealed that students' academic self-efficacy was developed through active involvement in discussions, presentations, question-and-answer sessions, and group activities; the provision of motivation and appreciation; the encouragement of independent learning; and the creation of a supportive learning environment that encouraged students to ask questions and express their opinions. Teachers also played important roles as learning planners, facilitators, motivators, feedback providers, and evaluators, helping students recognize their abilities and build confidence in facing academic challenges. In conclusion, the development of students' academic self-efficacy in the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum is supported by active learning strategies and the optimal involvement of teachers in creating a learning environment that promotes students' independence, participation, and confidence in their academic abilities.

papers.title: Probabilistic Operating-Error Forecasting for 10 kV Instrument Transformers Using Intrinsic Variation–Trend Decomposition and Multi-Kernel Deep Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting of ratio and phase errors of 10 kV current transformers (CTs) is difficult under distorted and time-varying conditions due to mixed harmonics, ambient-driven drifts, and limited reference-grade field data. This paper proposes a reference-free probabilistic framework for CT operating-error forecasting. First, three-phase secondary waveforms from multiple CTs on the same electrical branch are converted into synchronized phasors, and relative ratio and phase errors are estimated under the common primary current assumption. Then, intrinsic variation–trend decomposition (IVD) separates each error sequence into high-frequency disturbances, medium-frequency operating components, and low-frequency trends, forming an interpretable multiscale representation. Finally, modal features and meteorological variables are fused and fed into a kernel deep Gaussian process (KDGP) model to capture nonlinear, periodic, and trend-related error patterns and generate probabilistic forecasts with adaptive confidence intervals. Experiments on real 10 kV field data show that the proposed IVD–KDGP achieves lower root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) than representative deep learning, decomposition-based, and Gaussian process baselines for three-phase ratio- and phase-error forecasting. It also provides well-calibrated prediction intervals and low continuous ranked probability scores (CRPS), showing its effectiveness in both point forecasting and uncertainty quantification. The proposed method offers a practical tool for online error tracking, prioritized calibration, and long-term power quality management of CTs.

papers.title: A Review of Intelligent Hybrid Vehicle Control Unit and a Proposed ESP32-Based ECU Framework for an Educational Hybrid Electric Vehicle Trainer
papers.abstract: An electronic control unit (ECU) in a hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) receives information from sensors, evaluates the vehicle operating condition, and selects suitable control states through an energy-management strategy (EMS). The choice of control method affects decision quality, response, computational demand, and implementation cost. This paper reviews recent HEV energy-management research published from 2022 to 2026, with emphasis on rule-based control, reinforcement learning, deep reinforcement learning, model predictive control, and low-cost hardware validation. The Ten relevant journal studies are compared according to their control approach, input information, validation method, reported contribution, and limitations. The review indicates that learning- and prediction-based methods can improve optimisation under varying driving conditions, but often depend on detailed models, training data, or host-computer resources. Rule-based control remains attractive where transparency, predictable execution, and low implementation complexity are important. Based on these findings, a input– decision–output using an ESP32 microcontroller is presented for an educational HEV trainer. The ECU accepts driver-demand, vehicle-state, battery-state, and safety-related inputs; applies sensor validation and priority-based decision rules; and produces operating-mode and warning outputs for display. It defines a technically grounded architecture and a future validation plan. The main contribution is to connect recent HEV EMS research with a simple, transparent, and potentially low-cost embedded ECU suitable for educational demonstration.

papers.title: Data-Driven Design and Optimization of TPMS Structures: A Critical Review of Deep Learning, Inverse Design, and Multiscale Engineering Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures provide a compact geometric platform for tailoring mechanical, thermal−hydraulic, transport, and energy absorption behaviors, but their coupled design space makes repeated numerical evaluation expensive, particularly for functionally graded and multiscale structures. Data-driven methods have therefore been increasingly used to approximate structure−property relationships and accelerate design exploration. This review critically examines how machine learning and deep learning are being used for TPMS design, with an emphasis on forward property prediction, inverse and generative design, surrogate-assisted optimization, and multiscale topology optimization. Studies from a documented search were classified by the role, demonstrated architecture, and reported validation level. Rather than treating model accuracy as the primary measure of progress, the review compares the reported approaches in terms of training-data requirements, extrapolation behavior, computational savings, design variables, physical constraints, manufacturability, and validation against high-fidelity simulation or experiment, and it separates results obtained on TPMS structures from methods transferred from strut, shell, spinodoid, and other architectures. Most TPMS models are tested on random splits within the sampled design space; few test extrapolation, and where this has been done, failure-related quantities degraded more than elastic properties. In the examples examined, the largest reported gains coincide with functionally graded designs and expanded spatial design freedom, but no study separates the contributions of geometry, search algorithm, and learning model under controlled conditions. Common limitations are the lack of shared benchmark problems, inconsistent simulation and homogenization assumptions, limited treatment of manufacturing variability, uncalibrated uncertainty estimates, and insufficient comparison with classical optimization under equivalent computational budgets. The review therefore positions data-driven methods as acceleration and design-exploration tools rather than replacements for physics-based analysis and established optimization methods, and it proposes a design workflow with explicit rules for accepting a prediction, requesting a high-fidelity evaluation, and accounting for manufacturing deviations.

papers.abstract: Abstract To address the limitations of conventional Fusion Entropy (FE) in rotating machinery fault diagnosis, including time-frequency energy dispersion, insufficient noise robustness, and limited capability of single-scale analysis to characterize complex signal dynamics, this study first proposes a novel Phase Consistency Fusion Entropy (PCFE) method. Specifically, the Synchrosqueezing Transform (SST) is employed to improve time-frequency energy concentration and resolution, while phase consistency (PC) information is incorporated to weight the time-frequency energy distribution, thereby capturing both energy and phase-structural information. To extend PCFE to multiscale complexity analysis and improve the stability of entropy estimation, a Refined Composite Multiscale (RCM) strategy is subsequently incorporated to establish the refined composite multiscale phase consistency fusion entropy (RCMPCFE). Bayesian optimization is further employed to optimize the hyperparameters of the Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier for fault identification. Simulation results demonstrate that RCMPCFE exhibits good discriminative capability and stability. On the two real-world fault datasets, RCMPCFE achieves classification accuracies of 99.67% and 99.58%, respectively, substantially outperforming conventional methods.

papers.abstract: This paper addresses the tracking problem of hypersonic variable-sweep vehicles (HVSVs) subject to model uncertainties and feedback gain perturbations. Neglecting feedback gain perturbations in controller design can degrade tracking performance and compromise control reliability. To address this issue, a non-fragile tube model predictive control (MPC) method is proposed in this paper. A polytopic linear parameter-varying model is established to describe the vehicle’s dynamics. The reliable tracking control is designed within the tube MPC framework, integrating a non-fragile robust feedback control law and a nominal MPC term. Sufficient conditions are derived for designing the feedback gain under prescribed gain perturbations. By the resulting non-fragile control law, it has been analyzed that the tracking errors between the actual vehicle system and the nominal vehicle system are constrained to the computed robust positively invariant set under perturbed feedback control. In the nominal MPC layer, the feedforward control inputs are obtained by solving a quadratic programming problem with tightened constraints, which is formulated based on the nominal vehicle system. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve steady and accurate trajectory tracking with the enhancement of reliability to perturbed feedback control during the process of variable sweep wing.

papers.title: Tensor-Product Legendre Features for Physics-Informed Neural Networks: A Fixed-Time Evaluation on Nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) provide a framework for approximating solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs), but their accuracy depends on the input representation and optimization procedure. We investigated a Legendre-expanded PINN (LE-PINN) that constructs tensor-product Legendre features from space–time inputs before processing them with a multilayer perceptron. LE-PINN and a standard PINN were evaluated on viscous Burgers, nonlinear Klein–Gordon, and nonlinear Schrödinger problems under fixed training-time budgets, with results reported over 10 randomized trials. For the Burgers problem, LE-PINN achieved a lower mean relative L2 error, mean squared error, maximum absolute error, and PDE residual RMS. For Klein–Gordon, it achieved a lower mean relative L2 error and mean squared error, but a higher maximum absolute error and residual RMS. For the nonlinear Schrödinger problem, the standard PINN achieved lower mean values for all four metrics. We additionally reported an Ulam–Hyers-motivated empirical error-to-residual ratio when an exact reference solution is available. Although this ratio was lower for LE-PINN in all three problems, a smaller ratio can result from a larger residual and does not establish an improved accuracy or a certified stability bound. The results demonstrate the problem-dependent benefits and limitations of tensor-product Legendre features under the evaluated computational budgets.

papers.abstract: This study investigates short-term natural gas consumption forecasting in the city of Ternopil and the contribution of different feature groups to forecasting accuracy. Synchronized natural gas consumption and meteorological observations from 2007 to 2019 were used. A total of 203 calendar, meteorological, and derived features were constructed. Six machine learning models, three naive baseline forecasts, and a seasonal ETS model were compared. Hyperparameters were optimized using Optuna, model performance was evaluated using six temporal folds with an expanding training window, and final testing was conducted on data from 2019. XGBoost achieved the lowest mean root mean squared error of 4307.13 ± 280.29 m3 across the cross-validation folds and a root mean squared error of 6517.29 m3 on the test set. No statistically significant difference was found between XGBoost and Random Forest, although both models outperformed the baseline forecasts. Feature ablation analysis showed that adding historical gas consumption features to calendar features reduced the mean root mean squared error by 81.42%. Adding meteorological features to a feature set that already included consumption history further reduced this error by 0.51%. Among the features evaluated for XGBoost, gas consumption 24 h before the target interval had the highest mean absolute SHAP value. The adaptive online conformal method produced prediction intervals that contained the observed consumption in 89.32% of cases, compared with a nominal coverage level of 90%. However, these intervals had the largest mean width among the prediction interval methods considered. The findings are limited to forecasting for a single city and one test year.

papers.abstract: This paper proposes a distributed model predictive control (DMPC) scheme with preview disturbance based on bargaining game theory for the active suspension control of a light rail vehicle (LRV). The objective is to improve ride comfort and safety by minimizing the deflection of suspension system and the vertical acceleration of the car bodies. The LRV is modeled as a multi-body dynamical system consisting of two power carbodies and one trailer carbody. The proposed DMPC framework decomposes the vehicle into three dynamically interacting subsystems, each governed by a local MPC controller. The optimal control inputs are determined by formulating the control problem as a bargaining game, which is then solved by a negotiation algorithm. The proposed approach is evaluated through numerical simulations under sinusoidal track disturbances and compared with a centralized MPC scheme. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DMPC effectively attenuates vertical acceleration and suspension deflections, thereby enhancing ride comfort and operational safety while achieving superior overall control performance. These findings indicate that the proposed DMPC provides an effective and computationally attractive alternative to centralized MPC.

papers.title: FEMORAL NECK FRACTURE MANAGEMENT IN ELDERLY PATIENTS
papers.abstract: Background: Femoral neck fractures represent a major global health challenge, with international one-year mortality rates ranging from 20% to 30% and caseloads projected to nearly double by 2050. Because the intra-capsular environment relies on a tenuous retrograde blood supply from the medial femoral circumflex artery, displaced fractures carry a severe risk of avascular necrosis and nonunion. Objective: To outline an efficient, evidence-based clinical pathway for the perioperative management, surgical decision-making, and secondary prevention of femoral neck fractures to optimize patient outcomes. Methods: We synthesize current evidence regarding injury classification (emphasizing the high mechanical instability of Pauwels Type III shear angles), rapid pre-operative optimization, tailored surgical interventions, enhanced recovery protocols, and secondary fracture prevention. Results: Pre-operative Care: Prioritizes clinical stabilization for surgery within 24–48 hours, multimodal analgesia incorporating scheduled NSAIDs to limit systemic opioids, and aggressive correction of reversible deficits (e.g., anemia, dehydration) without procedural delay. Surgical Management: Displacement dictates intervention, making primary arthroplasty the standard of care. Hemiarthroplasty minimizes operative time and blood loss for lower-demand, frail patients, whereas Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA) provides superior long-term functional scores for highly active individuals. Choice of surgical exposure balances visualization (posterior approach), stability (lateral approach), and anatomical preservation (direct anterior approach). Post-operative Care & Recovery: An Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocol targets mobilization within 24 hours, chemical thromboprophylaxis, and nutrition. Safe discharge requires stable oral pain control and independent mobility with an assistive device. Secondary Prevention: Mandates bone density assessments, calcium and Vitamin D optimization, and formal fall prevention training. Conclusion: Implementing a standardized, multidisciplinary pathway focused on timely surgical intervention, appropriate arthroplasty selection, early mobilization, and secondary fracture prevention is essential for mitigating mortality and maximizing functional recovery in patients with femoral neck fractures.

papers.title: Characterizing the Edge of Stability in Variational Training Without Priors
papers.abstract: Variational approaches in deep learning promise to deliver improved uncertainty quantification and out-of-distribution generalization by inferring a distribution over weights, regularized by a divergence to a chosen prior. However, prior elicitation presents a significant challenge in deep learning, resulting in the common practice of significantly downweighting the regularization term in the variational objective. Recently, it was proposed to train solely via the expected loss by relying on implicit regularization from the optimizer, rather than explicit regularization from the divergence to the prior. While this approach largely sidesteps the issue of prior elicitation, current theory lacks an understanding of how key optimization hyperparameters impact the implicit regularization. Here, we theoretically and empirically demonstrate that larger learning rates and fewer parameter samples lead to flatter minima of the loss landscape, which are known to generalize better. We show that training on the expected loss operates at a modified edge of stability, characterized by the signal-to-noise ratio of the gradient estimates and the number of Monte Carlo samples. Experiments on out-of-distribution benchmark datasets confirm the practical significance of the theoretical results.

papers.title: Data-driven Correction Reduced-Order Stochastic Collocation Method for the Time-Dependent Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: We develop two hybrid data-driven Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) Reduced-Order Models (ROMs) for the non-stationary incompressible Navier--Stokes Equations (NSEs) with random viscosity. The proposed framework combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) ROMs, spatial filtering, data-driven closure modeling, and the Stochastic Collocation Method (SCM). A key feature is the approximation of the realization-dependent closure term by the closure associated with the expected viscosity. Consequently, a single data-driven closure model constructed from the full-order solution corresponding to the expected viscosity can be reused across all realizations, thereby avoiding the expensive construction of realization-specific closure models. This leads to the Data-Driven Correction UQ ROM (DDC-UQ-ROM) and its physically constrained variant, the Constrained DDC-UQ-ROM (CDDC-UQ-ROM), in which physical constraints are imposed on the data-driven correction model.   The proposed methods are evaluated for a two-dimensional (2D) flow past a circular cylinder problem with a 5D random viscosity field, considering mean Reynolds numbers $Re=100$ and $Re=500$, different correlation lengths, and both in-sample and out-of-sample parameter settings. Numerical results show that the DDC-UQ-ROM generally improves upon the standard Galerkin ROM (G-ROM), while the CDDC-UQ-ROM exhibits the most accurate and robust approximation of the benchmark energy evolution across the cases considered. The robustness and accuracy of the CDDC-UQ-ROM are further assessed through statistical error analyses of the first- and second-order energy moments, reduced-training-data experiments, and an indicative comparison of wall-clock computational costs with the full-order UQ calculations.
