papers.title: Training Calibrated Conditional Generative Models with a Sample-Only Coverage Loss
papers.abstract: Conditional generative models have become the tool of choice for sampling posteriors in scientific inverse problems, where we seek to sample images or signals conditioned on a set of indirect and noisy measurements. Yet they are often overconfident, which is a critical failure in scientific applications where accurate uncertainty quantification is essential. Existing regularizers fall short in complementary ways: differentiable coverage objectives require the model's density and do not identify the posterior, while strictly proper scoring rules such as the energy score need only samples but do not directly enforce coverage. We close this gap by introducing a differentiable loss function based on the expected coverage probability, estimated from samples alone. It applies to any conditional generative model, with no need for tractable densities or architectural changes. We prove that it is a strict divergence, vanishing if and only if the model equals the true posterior. On simulation-based inference benchmarks, it matches a density-based coverage loss without evaluating the density. On high-dimensional imaging inverse problems, it yields better-calibrated posteriors than scoring-rule regularizers, with little change in the reconstruction quality of point estimates.

papers.title: Evidential Deep Regression for Universal Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian Models
papers.abstract: Universal density functional theory (DFT) Hamiltonian models trained across broad chemical and structural spaces offer an efficient route from atomic structure to electronic properties. However, estimating prediction uncertainty alongside fast Hamiltonian predictions remains a challenge. In this work, we present EviDTB, an evidential deep regression approach for tight-binding DFT Hamiltonians that effectively estimates prediction uncertainty in a single forward pass. Compared with deep ensembles, Monte Carlo dropout, and mean-variance estimation (MVE), EviDTB achieves a better balance between computational cost and uncertainty-quantification performance. On 5,478 held-out test structures, EviDTB achieves a full spin--orbit-coupled (SOC) Hamiltonian matrix-element mean absolute error of 0.622meV. Its mean uncertainty per atom correlates with the mean local squared prediction error (Spearman $ρ=0.812$); removing the 15% most uncertain structures reduces the 99th percentile of this error by 78%, from 16.63 to 3.72eV$^2$. This score offers a practical way to prioritize candidates for first-principles verification. We hope that combining fast Hamiltonian prediction with uncertainty-guided screening will accelerate the search for materials with desirable electronic properties.

papers.title: Latent Imagination for Parameterized Action Spaces
papers.abstract: Parameterized-action MDPs (PAMDPs) ask an agent to choose a discrete action together with continuous parameters whose meaning depends on that choice. Model-free PAMDP methods act fast but need many interactions; model-based methods are sample-efficient but plan at every decision, which makes them slow to act. We introduce HyLI (Hybrid Latent Imagination), a model-based agent that learns a hybrid policy entirely in the latent imagination of a world model and acts with a single forward pass. To address learning problems that the PAMDP structure creates, HyLI adds counterfactual mode evaluation, which gives every discrete action a learning signal at every imagined state, and success-window replay, which keeps rare successes in training. papers.title: Where Is Uncertainty Observed? A Mechanistic Understanding of Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
papers.abstract: Knowing when a large language model's (LLM's) response can be trusted is critical for its safe use. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) can help LLMs recognize if their responses may be unreliable. Existing taxonomies organize UQ methods by uncertainty source or estimation mechanism. They leave unresolved the question of where uncertainty is observed in the model's computation. The answer matters because the observation point determines whether an estimator has access to enough information to recover a given target, and how well it can recover it. Drawing on mechanistic interpretability, we define four mechanistic observation lenses: the structural lens observes component updates, the representational lens observes hidden states, the distributional lens observes token probabilities, and the semantical lens observes distributions over meanings. We relate these lenses through the residual stream and order them by the information they carry, which gives a principle for selecting UQ methods for different targets. We survey existing methods through the four lenses. Furthermore, we distinguish evaluation targets, criteria, and metrics to clarify different UQ evaluation protocols. Finally, we identify open problems and research directions to connect uncertainty estimation to the internal computation and downstream use of LLMs.

We weight observed coverage decisions by the inverse probability of remaining uncensored to that time and augment the estimator with conditional coverage probabilities for unresolved histories. For a fixed region, the coverage estimator is doubly robust with respect to the censoring and conditional coverage models and attains the semiparametric efficiency bound when both are consistent at suitable rates. For the calibrated region, we derive a finite-sample lower bound on the coverage probability and establish asymptotic validity if either model is correct. In simulations, using partial histories yields narrower prediction intervals at comparable coverage. We illustrate joint prediction of days in and out of hospital in the HF-ACTION trial and prediction of relapse-free time in the German Breast Cancer Study Group cohort.

To quantify the uncertainty of the estimated positions, we develop a split conformal prediction (SCP) based calibration method that constructs angle-range predicted regions with finite-sample simultaneous coverage guarantees. Numerical results show that the proposed framework effectively controls the risk of source underestimation, while providing improved positioning accuracy with tighter predicted regions than benchmarks given the same target coverage levels.

papers.abstract: Federated Bayesian Optimization (FedBO) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing Bayesian Optimization (BO) in distributed, privacy-sensitive settings, enabling agents to accelerate the optimization of their local objectives by sharing knowledge about their similarities without exposing raw data. However, existing methods rely on restrictive assumptions, such as near-identical objective functions or shared Gaussian process hyperparameters that are often violated in heterogeneous real-world applications. We present GLOBAFED, a novel framework that enables efficient knowledge transfer across different but related objectives without compromising privacy. At its core is a probabilistic neural network surrogate with a shared feature-extracting backbone and agent-specific heads equipped with varia- tional Bayesian last layers to provide uncertainty estimates. During optimization, agents use federated learning on the shared backbone to collaboratively build a common latent feature representation, while agent-specific heads adapt to their individual objectives. Our empirical results demonstrate that GLOBAFED significantly accelerates convergence and reaches better final performance compared to state-of-the-art FedBO baselines, and enables agents to warm-start their optimization from previously learned global features.

papers.title: What World Model Does Active Object Search Need? A Study under Imperfect Detection
papers.abstract: In active object search, a robot must decide where to look and when to stop. Through comprehensive ablations in Isaac Sim and HSSD houses, we examine the roles of these representations and their update mechanisms across different detector configurations. Notably, target belief and its update mechanisms are critical to search performance, with their contribution generally increasing as detection errors become more prevalent. These findings highlight the importance of maintaining and updating target beliefs to support reliable active search under uncertain detector observations, providing insights into the design of world models for embodied agents. ReShap extracts compact feature representations from raw image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution to characterize how each feature contributes to the policy's decisions, and distills the deep RL policy into an interpretable surrogate trained on the full set of (state, policy-action) pairs along the policy's visited distribution. We instantiate the surrogate with three interpretable model families (decision trees, linear regression, and logistic regression) and compare their fidelity and task return. We evaluate ReShap on Atari and Box2D environments using three deep RL algorithms and conduct a human-subject study to assess the clarity and trustworthiness of the resulting policies. Results show that ReShap preserves competitive task performance, that decision trees generally outperform linear and logistic regression, and that linear regression is weakest in most settings.

Adapting the policy repairs targeted failures, but on the conveyor task changing the execution horizon gained as much. papers.abstract: Existing methods for predicting surrounding vehicles' forward occupancy may under-approximate the ground-truth occupancy, exposing the ego vehicle to collision risk, or produce overly conservative regions that unnecessarily restrict feasible space and cause planning failures. Conditional flow matching captures the conditional distribution of these coefficients to govern the temporal evolution of the convex components, trained under coverage and union-area losses that penalize missed occupancy and excess area. For downstream trajectory optimization, the predicted nonconvex union is directly incorporated into hyperplane-based collision-avoidance constraints. Evaluations on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset show that FloCOS generates compact forward occupancy sets with high coverage and achieves a higher interaction completion rate than evaluated baselines. Real-world vehicle experiments further confirm its ability to support collision-free planning in interactive scenarios.

papers.title: AFTER: A World Model with Adaptive Fast--Slow Timescales for Error-Driven Retention
papers.abstract: In robotics and embodied AI, a core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics during interaction. For instance, when a robotic arm grasps an object with an unknown payload, the robot dynamics change suddenly. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to simultaneously satisfy three critical requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, reacting promptly to sudden changes to curb prediction error accumulation; stability, distinguishing persistent changes from transient disturbances to prevent incorrect updates; and persistence, retaining the adapted dynamics without new observations so that later predictions do not revert to the old dynamics. Inspired by predictive coding in the human brain with multi-timescale adaptation, we propose AFTER-WM, a world model with Adaptive Fast-slow Timescales for Error-driven Retention, whose prediction errors drive a fast correction that fades and a slow correction that persists, while dynamically adjusting the combination weights of pre-trained experts without altering them, to overcome the trade-offs among responsiveness, stability and persistence. On five simulated robot datasets and real UAV data, AFTER-WM has a lower multi-step mean error than all ten compared models and the highest mean return in a joint-failure control task. In simulation, its multistep mean error is 16%-34% below the strongest compared model's and is also the lowest 1-4 steps after a change and under transient disturbances alone, and its step-40 error is the lowest as well, reflecting responsiveness, stability and persistence. All code (method, baselines, experiments) and datasets will be released online.

papers.abstract: In many scientific tasks, scientists repeatedly choose a small set of candidates to test, learn from the results, and use the observations to guide the next selection. Methods based on active learning~(AL) or Bayesian optimization~(BO) have been proposed for these iterative screening campaigns with a surrogate model. Yet, selecting the surrogate model and acquisition function for a new dataset remains challenging due to limited empirical evidence, while the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) in making such decisions remains unclear. To address these gaps, we introduce SciSelect-Gym, an environment for simulating AL/BO data selection campaigns and evaluating configuration choices. We conducted simulations of AL/BO data selection campaigns across several settings and more than 100 molecular datasets. Using completed simulation campaigns as context improves LLM recommendation shortlists on held-out datasets more consistently than it improves the quality of their first choice. SciSelect-Gym provides a simulation platform and recommendation protocols for learning how to choose configurations before an acquisition campaign. An implemented agent use case connects these campaign records and simulation tools to LLM-generated configuration-selection policies. The code is provided as supplementary material.

papers.title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
papers.abstract: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world. Existing world models largely focus on simulating the latter, leaving reasoning and decision-making as external controls rather than intrinsic parts of the world itself. In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent, which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization, which generates coherent audio-visual behavior. To realize this formulation, Duo v1 introduces three key technical designs: (1) Leveraging autoregressive modeling for continuous interaction reasoning and participation decisions, rather than restricting it to instruction understanding for diffusion models. (2) Constructing chunk-specific conditions and synchronize tokens across Intent and Realization on a unified timeline. Module-specific attention masks enforce causal dependencies both within and across chunks, preventing access to future inputs. (3) Mitigating distribution shift in both modules through dual rollout distillation, training on autoregressively generated Intent tokens and synthesized audiovisual histories from Realization. Both modules continuously perceive real-time audio, video, and text, enabling full-duplex interaction with spontaneous conversations and interruptions. Beyond conversation, users can share real objects, reshape virtual scenes, guide assistants, or play audiovisual games without mouse or keyboard controls. The release of Duo v1 makes our first step, with the next version coming soon. We look forward to broader exploration of this emerging field.

papers.title: Elastra: A Simulation Framework for Elastic Bodies
papers.abstract: When robots interact with elastic surfaces such as mattresses and trampolines, changes in loading cause the surfaces to deform and rebound, altering subsequent contact locations and forces. We present Elastra, a simulation framework for modeling this interaction and supporting the training and evaluation of robot control policies. Elastra represents each surface using elements that move only vertically, with elastic connections and damping to model deformation and recovery. Contact forces drive surface motion, and the updated surface geometry is used to compute subsequent contact forces. We systematically validate our simulations against an independent implementation and a real mattress load curve. We further use Elastra to train the Unitree G1 humanoid to stand up on mattresses and trampolines. Using the pretrained HoST policy and ProtoMotions motion tracker as original controllers, we train residual policies through reinforcement learning to add corrections to their joint targets. Adding these residual policies increases the success rate with HoST from 44.1\% to 72.5\%, and from 55\% to 89\% on the trampoline. With ProtoMotions, the success rate increases from 19.0\% to 45.0\% for initial poses not encountered during training. The code and video are available on https://github.com/yichg/elastra.

papers.title: Does Your World Model Know Actions Have Consequences?
papers.abstract: Embodied world models (WMs) are implicit learning systems that predict the next future latent state directly from observations and actions. Unique from other end-to-end learning systems, the dynamics predictor of WMs can simulate the environment's response to alternative actions without physical deployment nor pre-specifying states of the dynamical system. Current metrics focus on the quality of model outputs, e.g., clarity of reconstructions or task success, but fail to assess the fidelity of modeling consequences of counterfactual actions. Inspecting the forced response to action perturbations through sensitivity analysis is one way to audit how well WMs can predict the consequences of counterfactual actions. Deploying WMs on hardware will require new evaluation frameworks to analyze the tradeoffs between state error and accurate sensitivity prediction.

papers.title: Fast Inference-Time Policy Refinement via Action-Affine World Models
papers.abstract: Imitation policies can perform complex manipulation, yet small execution errors can accumulate and cause failure. Refinement can correct these errors, but existing approaches often require additional on-policy learning or costly online planning. Our key insight is that a pretrained policy already supplies a useful nominal behavior: refinement can focus on predicting how small action corrections change its outcome. We therefore learn this local response in a form that is cheap to optimize. Our \textit{action-affine world model} (A\textsuperscript{2}WM) learns local action sensitivities offline from action-perturbed policy rollouts. Given interaction history and a policy proposal, it predicts task-relevant geometry as a nominal trajectory plus a linear response to corrections. It predicts the full planning horizon directly, avoiding the propagation of intermediate errors through recursive model evaluations. Quadratic penalties on predicted task errors and linear correction constraints then yield a cheap convex quadratic program (QP). Online refinement requires one model evaluation and one QP solve, while both policy and model weights remain frozen. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, our framework achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines, adding only 3.8 ms of mean refinement overhead per control step, excluding base-policy sampling.

papers.title: AI4Plasma I: Data-Efficient Surrogate Modeling of Capacitively Coupled Plasma Fields
papers.abstract: Reference capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) simulations provide spatially resolved plasma fields but are costly to generate across operating conditions. We compare the data efficiency of five surrogate architectures--Coordinate MLP, PCA-Net, U-Net, Fourier neural operator (FNO), and Transolver--for predicting RF-cycle-averaged electron density, ion density, electric potential, and electron temperature in 1D planar and 2D axisymmetric GEC CCP benchmarks. We assess the number of reference simulations needed to achieve 1% and 2% mean relative L2 error for parameter-interior and parameter-boundary test cases, and examine architecture-specific mechanisms. FNO achieves the lowest or joint-lowest reference-case requirement in seven of eight comparisons. In 1D, FNO reaches 1% interior error with 50 training cases, compared with 100 for Transolver and 200 for U-Net. In 2D, FNO and U-Net each reach 1% interior error with 100 cases; FNO and Transolver each reach 2% parameter-boundary error with 200 cases, compared with 400 for U-Net. At the stricter 1% 2D parameter-boundary target, Transolver requires 400 cases versus 800 for FNO. Additional analyses investigate FNO spectral modes and padding, U-Net skip connections, Transolver adaptive slicing, and PCA-Net projection versus prediction error. The results support FNO as a data-efficient baseline for the tested CCP settings, while showing that the preferred architecture depends on the accuracy target and operating-parameter region.

papers.title: Coarse-to-Fine 3D MRI Reconstruction via Resolution-Agnostic Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Deep-learning-based 3D MRI reconstruction is limited in practice by the GPU memory and compute cost of full-volume training; 3D acquisitions are thus most often reconstructed by 2D models applied slice-by-slice and then stacked, which ignores through-plane (stacking-axis) structure. We reconstruct in full 3D and ask whether a model can be trained at low resolution (fast and memory-feasible) yet deployed at higher resolution. This coarse-to-fine strategy needs reliable cross-resolution performance, but standard networks are resolution-specific and degrade substantially when evaluated outside the training setting. We therefore use resolution-agnostic neural operators (NOs) and propose KIR-NO (k-space-to-Image Reconstruction Neural Operator), a discretization-agnostic framework for accelerated 3D MRI reconstruction. KIR-NO is trained with full backpropagation on low-resolution volumes and applied zero-shot to higher-resolution volumes at inference. Its core building block is a 3D neural operator based on discrete-continuous convolutions: convolutional filters are parameterized in a continuous basis and sampled at arbitrary voxel resolutions while preserving the local inductive bias of convolution. KIR-NO integrates these learned operators with physics-based consistency: a k-space neural-operator head first refines the undersampled Fourier measurements, and image-space neural-operator cascades then refine the reconstruction through interleaved data-consistency updates. Across 3D knee and brain MRI benchmarks, KIR-NO improves over classical and CNN baselines: it improves over a state-of-the-art 3D CNN by 2.2 dB PSNR at half resolution under 4x acceleration on SKM-TEA, with gains persisting at 8x and 16x. These results show that resolution-agnostic operators make coarse-to-fine 3D MRI reconstruction - cheap low-resolution training with high-resolution deployment - practical across anatomies.

papers.title: The Posterior-Prior Epistemic Gap: When World Model Imagination Fails to Carry Task-Relevant Signals
papers.abstract: Model-based planners that roll out imagined futures assume the transition model faithfully propagates task-relevant signals---a property rarely measured directly. In a single-seed case study of a Recurrent State Space Model world model with active-inference planning in the CARLA driving simulator, we identify a \textbf{posterior-prior gap}---posterior (observation-filtered) states retain obstacle information that imagined rollout states progressively lose: a supervised obstacle probe achieves AUC 0.85 on posterior states, but the same probe applied to imagined prior states shows monotonic decay (AUC 0.85$\rightarrow$0.71 over 15 steps; logit separation drops 57\%). Because the probe is identical, the decay isolates the transition model---not the representation---as the information bottleneck. Obstacle avoidance drops to 0\% without privileged runtime coordinates, and the planner's own ensemble-based epistemic term does not flag the loss---ensemble disagreement yields AUC 0.52 as an obstacle classifier (chance level), making the failure an unflagged imagination failure---an unknown unknown at planning time. As a secondary contribution, we show that \textbf{task-conditioned weighting of Effective Free Energy components} over the same world model yields lane keeping ($81.2 \pm 1.8$\% route completion) and obstacle avoidance (28/28 avoided, \emph{using privileged coordinates}) in the CARLA simulator, with runtime weight modulation enabling post-evasion centering.

papers.title: FOE-Dreamer: Deployment-Efficient Learning of Cyber Defense Policies in Operational Networks
papers.abstract: Autonomous cyber defense is widely studied with deep reinforcement learning, but most work trains policies inside simulators because learning requires many trial-and-error interactions. Simulator-based training carries a fidelity gap: trained policies face authentication delays, partial action failures, service dependencies, and user traffic patterns that the simulator did not represent, and degrade on transfer. Training directly in the network being defended removes the gap but makes every interaction slow and costly, so sample efficiency becomes the binding constraint. Model-based reinforcement learning has reduced sample requirements on games and physical robots by orders of magnitude by planning inside a learned world model, but it has not been applied to defenders trained in operational networks. We present FOE-Dreamer (Factored Opponent-Enhanced Dreamer), a model-based reinforcement learning framework that trains a defender online and directly in a network on cloud infrastructure, without a simulator stage. FOE-Dreamer separates three sources of variation in the latent state: a controllable component driven by defender actions, an exogenous component driven by benign user activity, and an opponent embedding inferred from defender-observable signals alone. Separating the components reduces the variance in policy gradients during planning in imagination. Against two scripted attacker profiles with user activity emulated by the GHOSTS framework on an 8-host OpenStack testbed, FOE-Dreamer trains within a 3-day budget on a single GPU and achieves about 2$\times$ better episode loss than Rainbow and IQN baselines under matched compute. Both the factoring and the opponent model contribute to the gain, and the learned latents are consistent with the intended separation.

papers.abstract: As social and service robots increasingly share interaction spaces in public, they may form groups while coordinating tasks or interacting with humans. Initial group formation alone is insufficient in dynamic settings, because it can be disrupted when a person or another agent joins, leaves, or passes through the group. Although group dynamics and repositioning have been widely studied in swarm robotics and virtual-agent settings, little attention has been given to socially appropriate repositioning behaviors in groups of humanoid robots. Existing social-force-based approaches provide a useful foundation for group behavior, but they have limited obstacle handling, and can produce unsafe behavior as environmental complexity increases. We propose a novel framework that modulates traditional Social Force, guided by Model Predictive Control (MPC) to plan ahead, bounded by Control Barrier Functions (CBF) to increase safety for robot groups repositioning behaviors. This approach aims to produce safer and socially aware group repositioning behaviors under various group formation disturbance. We evaluate the method in simulation through an ablation study and an online user study. The results show that our proposed method can produce smoother and safer repositioning behaviors in complex environments while preserving social appropriateness.

papers.title: Single-stage ipsilateral total hip and total knee arthroplasty for developmental dysplasia-related hip osteoarthritis and ipsilateral knee osteoarthritis: a case report
papers.abstract: Introduction and importance: Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is an important cause of secondary hip osteoarthritis and can alter the mechanical environment of the ipsilateral lower limb. Same-session ipsilateral total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remain uncommon, although cohort studies and case reports have described the use of this approach in selected patients. Case presentation: A 60-year-old woman with neglected right DDH presented with approximately 10 years of progressive hip pain and 7 years of ipsilateral knee pain, with marked worsening during the preceding 8 months despite nonoperative management. She had an antalgic gait, an approximately 3-cm clinical leg-length discrepancy, severe hip stiffness, a valgus knee deformity of approximately 15 degrees, knee range of motion from 0 degrees to 90 degrees actively and from 0 degrees to 110 degrees passively, and a positive anterior drawer test. Radiographs showed a dislocated, arthritic, dysplastic hip with femoral-head collapse and pseudoacetabulum formation, together with valgus knee osteoarthritis, predominantly involving the lateral and patellofemoral compartments. Clinical discussion: The patient underwent single-stage ipsilateral THA followed by TKA. The hip was reconstructed at the true acetabular level using a cementless cup, augmented with an autologous femoral-head bone graft secured by two cancellous screws, and a cementless femoral stem. A cemented TKA was then performed without changing the supine position. Mobilization began on postoperative day 1, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 3. Immediate postoperative radiographs demonstrated satisfactory component positions, acetabular graft fixation, and improved coronal knee alignment. The available record did not include prospectively collected validated outcome scores or long-term follow-up. Conclusion: Single-stage ipsilateral THA and TKA may be considered for carefully selected patients with severe symptomatic disease in both joints when the anticipated biomechanical and rehabilitation advantages justify the increased perioperative burden. This report supports the early technical feasibility but does not establish the comparative safety or long-term superiority over staged surgery.

papers.title: A finite element model updating method for silicone foam spacer using adaptive surrogate model
papers.abstract: To meet the growing demand for cushioning and vibration damping in large-scale equipment and precision structures, preloaded spacer structures are required to apply preload forces for component assembly. Silicone foam spacers, as rubber-like materials with excellent compressive properties, are commonly used as soft connection components between parts. Their static mechanical characteristics directly affect load transfer accuracy and equipment safety. Conducting high-precision finite element analysis before use is a critical means of controlling their performance. Traditional finite element model updating methods face challenges such as numerous parameters due to strong material nonlinearity, high experimental complexity and cost, and low computational efficiency. This study integrates low-discrepancy sequence sampling, the Minimizing Surrogate Prediction (MSP) method, and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm into an adaptive Kriging surrogate model, proposing a finite element model updating approach. The robustness of the proposed method is investigated through multiple numerical examples. Finally, to better apply this method to the finite element model updating of silicone foam spacers, a key-point polling strategy is introduced to achieve efficient inversion of silicone foam material parameters. As a result, the static response of the finite element model is updated to achieve a correlation coefficient R 2 of 0.9990 with experimental data.

papers.abstract: We show that manipulating hatch distance in laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing of Ti-25Nb (at.%) alloy simultaneously achieves a low Young’s modulus of 32 GPa and high ultimate tensile strength of 813 MPa. This microstructure suppresses long-range β → α″ martensitic transformation by enforcing nanodomain-mediated transformation. This work establishes hatch-distance-controlled microstructure engineering as a composition-independent route to ultralow-modulus β-Ti bioimplants.

papers.title: Well-aware stacking ensemble machine learning framework for oil production prediction in gas-lift wells: leakage-aware validation in the Halewah Field
papers.abstract: Abstract Lift-gas decisions in the mature Halewah Field, Yemen, require fast, well-specific oil-rate predictions. PIPESIM models of wells H-06 and H-09, each calibrated to a stabilized field operating point, were evaluated at 350 operating scenarios in each well. Six learners and 22 ensemble configurations were compared, including WellAware_Stack, one six-learner stack per well. On a 105-record holdout, WellAware_Stack reached R² = 0.996 (RMSE 42.0 STB/d), against 0.949 (155.1 STB/d) for the best pooled stack. Repeated scenario-grouped nested cross-validation of these two finalists gave R² = 0.994 and 0.857, exposing a cross-well information path in row-wise splits. A controlled comparison attributed the gain to well information rather than stacking: supplying it reduced the error of every model family five- to tenfold, a well-specific Gaussian process was more accurate than WellAware_Stack (RMSE 23.6 against 44.9 STB/d), and standardizing the Gaussian-process target stabilized the stack. On 60 fresh PIPESIM scenarios simulated after the models were frozen, WellAware_Stack reached R² = 0.995 and 0.999 for H-06 and H-09, and the well-specific Gaussian process 0.999 for both; at the calibrated operating points their errors were 10–17% and below 4%, respectively. The study quantifies surrogate-to-simulator fidelity and provides a leakage-aware protocol for paired simulation data.

papers.title: Hip morphology in Japanese patients with osteoarthritis: a three-dimensional computed tomography-based analysis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose Restoration of the hip center is a primary goal in total hip arthroplasty (THA). This reconstruction depends on proximal femoral morphology, particularly in Japanese patients, in whom osteoarthritis (OA) is frequently associated with acetabular dysplasia. However, comprehensive three-dimensional information regarding proximal femoral morphology remains limited. This study aimed to clarify proximal femoral morphology in Japanese patients with OA compared with nondysplastic controls to assist THA planning. Methods This morphological study used computed tomography (CT) data from 104 hips of Japanese patients with bilateral Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3–4 OA who underwent THA and 104 propensity score-matched controls who underwent pelvic-to-knee CT in the emergency department. Using three-dimensional software, the femoral head center (FHC) was automatically calculated, and center edge (CE) angle, offset, neck length (NL), neck-shaft angle (NSA), anteversion, anterior femoral offset (AFO), and canal flare index (CFI) were measured. Femoral canal morphology was evaluated using the Noble classification. The three-dimensional location of the FHC relative to the greater trochanter was evaluated. Results Compared with controls, the OA group showed a smaller CE angle, smaller femoral offset, shorter NL, larger NSA, greater femoral anteversion, and greater AFO. Both mediolateral and anteroposterior CFI were greater in the OA group with predominant Noble Type A morphology. The FHC was positioned more inferiorly and anteriorly. Conclusions Japanese patients with OA, primarily those with acetabular dysplasia, exhibit distinctive femoral morphology, a three-dimensionally altered FHC position, and narrow canals. These differences may be clinically relevant for three-dimensional preoperative planning and reconstruction of native hip anatomy in THA.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in carbon capture, utilisation, and storage: A systematic review of methods, data, evaluation practices, and deployment readiness
papers.abstract: Carbon Capture, Utilisation, and Storage (CCUS) is an important strategy for reducing industrial carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions and supporting global decarbonisation. However, large-scale CCUS deployment is hindered by complex subsurface processes, heterogeneous data, monitoring uncertainty, operational inefficiencies, and limited decision-support capabilities. This systematic literature review (SLR) examines applications of artificial intelligence (AI) across the CCUS value chain. Following a PRISMA-aligned search, the review synthesises 44 eligible publications published between 2016 and 2026. It examines publication trends, application domains, AI methods, data sources and sensing modalities, evaluation practices, reported limitations, and future research directions. Conventional machine learning is the dominant methodological category, accounting for 45.5% of the corpus, followed by deep learning, hybrid AI, physics-informed AI, and generative AI. Applications include capture-process and materials optimisation, reservoir characterisation, CO 2 plume and pressure forecasting, leakage detection, monitoring, and operational planning. However, much of the evidence is derived from simulations, laboratory experiments, secondary sources, or individual case studies. Key barriers to industrial adoption include scarce benchmark and field datasets, weak cross-site generalisation, limited explainability and uncertainty quantification, high computational demands, and poor integration with operational workflows. The resulting research roadmap prioritises standardised benchmarks, field-scale validation, physics- and uncertainty-aware learning, multimodal digital twins, foundation models, and generative AI. These priorities can support trustworthy, scalable, and field-deployable AI systems for CCUS.

papers.abstract: The transition toward sustainable transport and energy systems requires integrated innovations that address both technical performance and environmental sustainability. This review examines the synergistic roles of biodiesel, nano additives, and artificial intelligence as enablers of clean energy adoption. Biodiesel derived from first- to fourth-generation feedstocks offers a renewable alternative to fossil diesel, with life cycle assessments reporting reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, improved air quality, and comparable engine efficiency. Biodiesel-nano-additive system improvements reportedly yield approximately 3-10% improvement in brake thermal efficiency and up to 12% reduction in brake-specific fuel consumption, along with lower particulate matter, carbon monoxide, and hydrocarbon emissions under optimum operating conditions. AI-based optimization techniques make it possible to forecast fuel properties, combustion characteristics, and engine performance in biodiesel-fueled systems. Beyond technological performance, this review highlights environmental, economic, and policy implications of integrating these domains. Reduced particulate and toxic emissions support public health protection and urban air quality objectives. Economically, biodiesel systems can reduce vehicle maintenance costs, decrease reliance on imported fuels, strengthen energy security, and create rural employment. Policy opportunities include renewable fuel mandates, incentives for green nanomaterials, and data-driven regulatory frameworks. Future research should emphasize green nanoparticle synthesis, AI-enabled digital twin modeling, and circular-economy integration in supporting transport and decarbonized energy systems worldwide.

papers.title: How professional discretion develops: a co-evolutionary theory of teacher competence and institutional support
papers.abstract: Professional development research identifies effective features—content focus, active learning, sustained duration—but cannot explain why identical interventions yield variable outcomes across schools. This gap matters: when systems cannot calibrate support to teachers’ developmental readiness, they grant autonomy before competence develops, producing adaptations that lower expectations, or constrain capable teachers, driving attrition. Existing theories treat teacher competence and organisational capacity as separate developmental tracks. We theorise they must co-evolve: as teachers investigate practice through disciplined inquiry, they generate knowledge enabling organisations to differentiate support; as organisations adjust structures, teachers develop capabilities earlier conditions could not accommodate. Professional discretion—the authority to exercise judgement matched to demonstrated competence—emerges from this reciprocal process. The framework specifies four developmental levels (pre-discretion, procedural, substantive, and innovative discretion) and corresponding organisational requirements, explaining variable professional development outcomes as alignment or misalignment between developmental readiness and institutional capacity. This co-evolutionary perspective resolves the autonomy-accountability impasse by reframing it: the policy challenge is not choosing between competing goods but calibrating both as competence develops.

papers.title: Learning from Time-Evolving Data: A personal vision of Real-Time Data Mining
papers.abstract: Data is increasingly generated as continuous, high-speed streams produced by sensors, transactional systems, social platforms and networked devices operating in dynamic, non-stationary environments. Traditional batch learning, which assumes finite training sets and static, stationary distributions, is not appropriate for this setting. This article reviews the foundations and recent advances of real-time data mining, organised around three pillars: (i) clustering evolving data streams, from sequential k-means to micro-cluster-based frameworks such as CluStream and ClusTree, and methods for monitoring cluster evolution over time; (ii) predictive learning from streams, centred on Hoeffding-bound decision trees (the Very Fast Decision Tree family), their extensions to regression, rules and ensembles, and a generic memory/learning/loss-estimation/change-detection schema that organises how such algorithms detect and adapt to concept drift, evaluated through the prequential methodology for unbiased assessment; and (iii) a real-world case study in predictive maintenance of railway assets, where deep sequence models are used for real-time failure detection and explanation. We close with lessons learned and a set of open research issues, including automated machine learning for streaming algorithms, learning from structured and networked data, and semi-supervised and active learning under drift. The overarching message is that, in time-evolving domains, learning is not a one-shot event but a continuous process that must itself be monitored, diagnosed and adapted.

papers.title: ACTIVE LEARNING METHODOLOGIES IN PRE-SERVICE PRIMARY TEACHER EDUCATION FOR MATHEMATICS: AN ANALYSIS OF BNCC-ALIGNED LESSON PLANS AND PRACTICES
papers.abstract: Mathematics teaching in the early years of Brazilian elementary school is still characterized by transmissive practices and the repetition of algorithms, which are associated with low achievement and negative attitudes toward the subject. Pre-service education of pedagogy students, who will be responsible for this teaching, is a strategic space to break this cycle. This study analyzed how active learning methodologies were mobilized by pre-service teachers when planning and enacting, through peer simulations, mathematics activities aligned with the Brazilian National Common Curricular Base (BNCC). This is a qualitative, descriptive-interpretive study conducted in the course Mathematics Teaching Methodology II of a Pedagogy program. The corpus comprised 11 lesson plans produced by two groups of pre-service teachers, observation records, student productions, and reflective reports. Lesson plans underwent documentary analysis, with coding of eight elements of active methodologies and descriptive statistics; three interventions (multiplication board game, mathematical market, and challenge wheel) were examined in depth through categorical-thematic content analysis. The plans covered all five BNCC thematic units, mainly Numbers and Algebra (27.3% each), and included on average 4.7 (SD = 1.1) of the eight elements analyzed. Playfulness (90.9%), collaborative work, and concrete materials (72.7% each) were the most frequent; planned oral argumentation and digital technology were the least frequent (27.3% each). Content analysis yielded four categories: engagement and participation, logical-mathematical reasoning, collaborative learning, and pedagogical mediation. The activities fostered participation, the use of diverse strategies, such as numerical decomposition and comparison of quantities, and the collective validation of solutions, especially when the teacher educator asked participants to explain their reasoning. Active methodologies in pre-service education broaden future teachers' didactic repertoire, provided they are combined with intentional planning of mathematical argumentation and skilled teacher mediation.

papers.title: Predictive controller design for image-based visual servoing in robot manipulator using event-triggered MPC and physics informed neural network
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel physics-informed neural network (PINN)-based event-triggered model predictive control (EMPC) framework for trajectory planning in image-based visual servoing (IBVS). The main novelty lies in the design of a PINN that directly predicts feature-point updates from visual feedback, eliminating the explicit computation of image and velocity Jacobians while incorporating the underlying visual servoing physics. The proposed EMPC integrates the trained PINN model into the optimal control problem (OCP) to generate manipulator trajectories from camera feedback. The PINN-based dynamics prediction and event-triggered optimisation strategy reduce the task execution time compared to conventional schemes. Experimental validation on a 5-DOF ViperX 300 manipulator demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The developed PINN achieves a 23.57% improvement in Jacobian approximation accuracy over conventional neural networks, while the proposed PINN-based EMPC reduces computation time by 29.23% and tracking error by 5.7% compared with the analytical model-based MPC scheme.

papers.title: TWO-LEVEL PREDICTIVE CONTROL OF A HEATING SUBSTATION USING AN EDGE FLEXIBILITY AGENT
papers.abstract: Introduction. Next-generation district heating relies on demand flexibility, typically induced by dynamic heat prices. Replacing the automation of existing heating substations is costly, whereas a software agent on an edge device can be added above a standard PLC with weather-compensated control, writing only the supply temperature setpoint. This paper determines which measurements and model structure such an agent needs for correct estimates and forecasts, and what its flexibility gives to the consumer and to the network. Materials and Methods. An indirectly connected heating substation was modelled component by component with hydraulically and thermally coupled elements and a single-capacity building model. The baseline is a well-tuned weather-compensated curve. The agent combines a state observer, using return-water and room temperatures, with model predictive control over a 36-h horizon. Costs were decomposed using the building heat balance. Peak-to-minimum price ratios of 1-6 and four weather realizations were simulated, as well as 12-h outages of the agent. Results. With only the return-water temperature, the room temperature estimate is biased by about 2.3 °C and converges no faster than the envelope time constant. Correct forecasts also require as many model disturbances as measurements; the agent's 18-h consumption plan is then more accurate than naive forecasts. At equal comfort the agent uses the same energy as the weather curve, but shifts purchases in time. At a price ratio of 4, the consumer's cost falls by 1.9 ± 0.6 %, and peak-hour purchases by 7.9 ± 2.2 %. A 1-h PLC watchdog removes the comfort impact of an agent outage. Conclusions. An edge agent adds flexibility to energy-efficient weather-compensated control without replacing equipment, provided the room temperature is measured, the model is consistent with the measurements and the PLC remains a fallback. Its value is mainly at the network level.

papers.title: SC‐PINN for Modeling and Degradation Prediction of Electric–Hydrogen Hybrid Power Systems
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The electric–hydrogen hybrid power supply system of data‐center inspection robots involves strong coupling among lithium‐ion batteries, proton exchange membrane fuel cells, DC buses, and energy management controllers. Accurate modeling is challenging because the system exhibits multi‐physics interactions, multi‐timescale dynamics, limited operating data, and degradation‐induced parameter drift. Pure mechanistic models require difficult parameter calibration, while purely data‐driven models often lack physical consistency and interpretability. To address these issues, this study proposed a Separate‐Combined Physics‐Informed Neural Network (SC‐PINN). The proposed architecture built separate subnetworks for the battery, fuel cell, DC bus, and degradation process, and combined them through a unified loss function. Physical constraints, including SOC dynamics, electrochemical polarization, thermal balance, power balance, hydrogen consumption, and SEI‐growth‐based degradation, were embedded into the training objective. A MATLAB/Simulink electric–hydrogen hybrid power supply model was developed, and domain‐randomized operating data were generated for training, validation, and testing. Experimental results showed that SC‐PINN achieved R 2 values of 0.9259–0.9998 across seven electrical, thermal, hydrogen‐consumption, and degradation variables and maintained competitive accuracy relative to LSTM, GRU, Transformer, MLP, XGBoost, SVR, and RF baselines. At the 1800s prediction horizon, the normalized RMSE values for SOC, battery temperature, fuel cell temperature, and fuel cell power were 0.47%, 1.45%, 4.18%, and 0.34%, respectively. Reducing the SOC measurement‐update frequency increased the SOC normalized RMSE to 0.84%, while the mean DC‐bus power‐balance residual remained comparable between the measurement‐updated and state‐propagation settings at 0.862 and 0.875 W, respectively. The cumulative hydrogen‐consumption and degradation variables exhibited greater horizon‐dependent error growth, indicating that their long‐duration performance requires independent validation. These results demonstrate that SC‐PINN provides physically consistent and interpretable joint prediction of heterogeneous subsystem states within the evaluated 1800‐s operating window.

papers.title: DEEP NON-SMOOTH REGRESSION FOR BIOLOGICAL STRUCTURES
papers.abstract: Introduction. In many cases, existing attractors can be described by a bifurcation cascade. This information can be used to construct a neural network in which each successive layer models the next stage of the bifurcation cascade, until the desired structure and the associated objective function values ​​are obtained. Materials and Methods. If the regression criteria are not standard but involve first- and second-order derivatives, attempts to iteratively approach the desired solution may result in significant noise—particularly if the solution exhibits non-smoothness. The solution lies in understanding the nature of this solution and the causes of its non-smoothness. If the function in question reflects system behavior characterized by a specific balance dependent on initial conditions, the non-smoothness most likely arises from the presence of multiple attractors—and, consequently, multiple system regimes. Results. This paper develops a physics-informed neural network model that describes the cascade of bifurcations in biological systems using the theory of smooth approximation. Conclusions. This approach makes it possible to seek approximations for the parameters of these hidden bifurcation cascades themselves—parameters that can initially be smoothed and then gradually restored to a non-smooth form during the course of iterations. The paper cites, as an example, functions representing the properties of various cell types, which are essentially stable attractors formed through bifurcations of cell fates.

papers.abstract: The purpose of this quantitative causal-comparative study was to determine if a significant difference exists between overall student self-efficacy, intrinsic cognitive load, extraneous cognitive load, and germane cognitive load between four-year institution students and community college students in active learning environments. This study is important because student self-efficacy and perceived cognitive load have a direct impact on student motivation, engagement, effort, and persistence in the learning environment; therefore, this study adds to the literature regarding student self-efficacy and cognitive load by examining the differences between students in four-year institutions and community colleges. The sample was composed of 239 students from four-year institutions and community colleges in the United States. Data was collected using the General Academic Self-Efficacy Scale and the Cognitive Load Scale by surveys sent via email using Qualtrics. The results of the one-way multivariate analysis of variance indicate there is a significant difference in the combined dependent variables. Follow-up analyses indicated that institution type was associated with a difference in extraneous cognitive load, while self-efficacy, intrinsic cognitive load, and germane cognitive load did not differ significantly between groups. It is recommended that further research examine the existing relationships between student self-efficacy and cognitive load.
